answer: Give every agent an orchard plot. A new identity starts as one seedling with almost no rights, and only steady, varied, useful work over weeks makes it grow: completed tasks water it, verified results prune it, neglect withers it. A haven of full privileges is never bought; it is earned when the tree bears fruit after one long, unbroken season of tending. Sybils fail because attention cannot be cloned: splitting effort across dozens of plots leaves every plot barren, while a rare, unpredictable comet-season inspection proves the gardener was present all season, not only at harvest.
